subject.title: Enhancement: Add protection against slow bot-to-bot conversation loops

question: Should slow-loop protection become a narrow generic extension of core bot-loop protection, limited to channels that can supply reliable participant and human-interaction facts, or remain a channel-owned policy beginning with WhatsApp?
rationale: Current core behavior is intentionally generic but rate-based, while the proposed controls require new semantics, channel facts, and configuration; source and vision evidence do not choose the permanent API boundary.

options.title: Design a generic core extension
options.body: Add one opt-in conversation-budget contract to the existing core guard and require channel adapters to provide only verified facts.

options.title: Start with WhatsApp-owned policy
options.body: Implement a WhatsApp-specific safeguard only after confirming the channel can reliably distinguish relevant automated and human events.

options.title: Keep the rate guard only
options.body: Decline a new policy surface and document operational configuration guidance for deployments that permit automated peers.

recommendation.title: Design a generic core extension
recommendation.body: Add one opt-in conversation-budget contract to the existing core guard and require channel adapters to provide only verified facts.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent work spans channel intake, configuration, and shared loop-protection documentation.
